justification: Real code change to the DCP extraction pipeline's section-boundary detection, shared by every council using the default (non-AI, non-page-range-configured) extraction path. Not Critical: additive-only guard extension, no existing behaviour changes for pages that were already handled correctly (verified by full-batch regression across all 39 already-committed CB chapters: 0 new artifact-scan bugs). Not Minor: it changes what content gets extracted for real pages, not just wording.

pre_impl.existing_data: Ran the real extractor against chapter-7-5's actual 122-page PDF (downloaded from R2) and printed every one of the 46 sections it produced, with real page ranges and content previews -- ground truth, not inference. Confirmed the existing TOC-page guard (_toc_hits >= 5) already correctly absorbs a chapter's FULL table-of-contents page. Traced the exact root cause of the remaining defect to a narrower case (a section's own mini-TOC divider page, 3-4 entries) that falls below that threshold.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Initially scoped this as 'fix the TOC-as-provision bug in chapter-7-5'. The real diagnosis showed TWO distinct defect classes: (1) section-divider mini-TOC contamination (clean, well-understood, fixed here) and (2) garbled map/key-site/legend pages producing scrambled text that section_re occasionally mismatches onto (a harder, separate problem, explicitly named as out-of-scope follow-up, not silently dropped or conflated with this fix).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extended the existing TOC-page guard with a second, narrower, independent signal rather than duplicating it or hardcoding to canterbury_bankstown -- the fix is general and will apply to any council using the default extraction path that has the same section-divider-page pattern (confirmed on TWO independent real chapters: chapter-7-5's pages 5/8/82 and chapter-11-15-marco-avenue's page 5).
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- reads already-downloaded/cached PDFs from R2, same mechanism proven throughout this investigation.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before this fix: a planner reading Canterbury-Bankstown chapter 1.1, 2.1 or 5.1 (or any future council/chapter sharing this layout pattern) would see a table-of-contents fragment and sibling section titles presented as if they were that section's actual regulatory text -- confusing and wrong, though not yet served in production for chapter-7-5 (it's one of the 13 held-back chapters). Separately discovered: chapter-11-15-marco-avenue (already LIVE, committed on PR #1045) IS currently serving exactly this defect on its '2.1 Objectives' provision -- flagged as a named, pending follow-up, not silently left in production nor auto-fixed without a decision.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_section_divider_guard.py -v ; python -m pytest -q ; python scripts/dq_check.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any of the 11 new tests fail if the guard's threshold or divider-marker logic regresses. dq_check.py fails if DQ-95's declared status and live result disagree.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 11/11 new tests pass, including 5 confusable-negative cases (real content page, garbled-map page with only 1 hit, 'section' mentioned mid-sentence, single-hit-with-marker below threshold, a marker appearing past the 300-char cutoff on a long real page) and 2 regression-pin cases for the pre-existing >=5 full-TOC guard. Full pytest suite: 4988 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (was 4977 before this branch's 11 new tests). Full-batch regression check (--all --review across all 39 already-committed CB chapters): 0 new artifact-scan bugs, exactly 1 real diff (chapter-11-15-marco-avenue's already-live '2.1' provision would be correctly removed, confirmed by direct diff inspection, not assumed). dq_check.py PASSED.

functions.name: is_toc_or_divider_page
functions.file_line: scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py (new, extracted from inline logic in _extract_sequential)
functions.input: page text (str), the council's section_re pattern
functions.output: bool -- True suppresses section detection on this page (its text is absorbed into the currently-open section) when either the full-TOC threshold (>=5 section-code matches) or the new divider threshold (a literal 'SECTION N' line in the first 300 chars plus >=2 matches) is met
functions.if_none: empty text -> 0 matches -> False (no suppression); this matches the pre-existing behaviour for the >=5 case exactly, since the function is a pure refactor of that logic plus one additive OR-branch

break_it.scenario: The new divider-marker check could false-positive on a real content page that happens to mention 'SECTION N' as a standalone line for a legitimate reason (e.g. quoting a cross-referenced chapter's own divider), incorrectly swallowing real content.
break_it.what_happens: A real provision could be silently dropped from what gets served.
break_it.how: Restricted the marker search to the first 300 characters of the page (real divider pages are short and the marker is always near the top; a long real page mentioning it deep in the body cannot trigger this) and required 2+ additional section-code matches on the SAME page as a second, independent confirming signal -- not the marker alone. Pinned with a dedicated test (test_section_divider_marker_deep_in_a_long_real_page_does_not_suppress) proving a >300-char real page with a late marker is NOT suppressed.

break_it.scenario: A code change to a shared extraction function used by every council could regress previously-clean chapters elsewhere, not just canterbury_bankstown.
break_it.what_happens: Silent content loss or corruption across the whole DCP corpus, not just the targeted chapter.
break_it.how: Ran the fixed extractor against ALL 39 already-committed canterbury_bankstown chapters (--all --review, memory-only) and diffed against the live, already-committed baseline: 0 new artifact-scan bugs, exactly 1 chapter shows any difference at all, and that difference is a confirmed correct improvement (removing 100% junk content), not a regression. This is the full-batch check this session's own prior lesson (a single-chapter spot check proves nothing) explicitly required.
break_it.repro: python scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py --council canterbury_bankstown --all --review, then diff the OVERALL SUMMARY provision counts per chapter against a live regulatory_provisions count query.

break_it.scenario: An earlier draft of the chapter-11-15-marco-avenue test used a truncated snippet copied from a diff report's preview text, silently asserting it was 'verbatim' when it was missing 2 of the page's 3 real section-code matches -- the test would have passed for the wrong reason (the real page has 3 hits, the truncated fixture had 1).
break_it.what_happens: A test that looks like it pins real behaviour but actually tests a fabricated, incorrect fixture -- exactly the class of false confidence this project's own QA discipline exists to catch.
break_it.how: Caught before committing: the test failed immediately when run (1 hit is below the >=2 threshold). Re-fetched the real PDF page directly and confirmed the true text (3 matches: 2.1/2.2/2.3), then rewrote the test with the verified real content and a note explaining the correction.
